guide.headline: Both offenses want to throw deep over leaky secondaries
guide.hook: Minnesota's deep ball against Miami's leaky secondary and a breakout pass rusher chasing the quarterback make this one worth the remote.

items.title: Vikings go over the top early
items.what: The Vikings rank No. 1 of 32 in pass explosiveness at 1.69, and the Dolphins rank No. 29 at limiting explosive passes at 1.46, a gap of 90 percentile points. This is not a lean, it is a mismatch. If Minnesota connects on a shot play, Miami has to change its coverage shell and the run game opens up behind it.
items.when: Watch the first deep shot of the game
items.who: Vikings deep passing vs Dolphins secondary

items.title: Dallas Turner hunting the quarterback
items.what: Dallas Turner already has 3.5 sacks, 12 QB hits, and two TFL this season, production that puts him in the top 4 percent of NFL linebackers. He is playing 84 percent of defensive snaps as the SLB on Minnesota's depth chart, and his per game production is up 138 percent from last season.
items.when: Watch third-and-medium when Miami's line has to pass block

items.title: Dolphins run game gets strangled
items.what: The Vikings rank No. 2 of 32 against the run at 27 percent allowed rush success rate, and the Dolphins rank No. 30 in rush success rate at 31 percent, a gap of 91 percentile points. Miami gets pushed into obvious passing downs, which is exactly where this Vikings defense makes its money.
items.when: Watch Dolphins yards per carry through the first quarter
items.who: Dolphins run game vs Vikings run defense

guide.cardLine: Two secondaries that cannot keep a lid on it meet a Vikings run defense that erases Miami's ground game.
